behavioral_effects: Compose long-syntax (mapping) volume entries of type volume or bind are now parsed into service volume facts instead of being silently dropped
Volume entries the extractor cannot parse are recorded in unknowns, matching the existing ports behaviour
The sandboxd workspace mount now references the x-sandbox-workspace-root anchor directly, ending the comment-discipline duplication the 2026-08-25 change record flagged as follow-up
compatibility_impact: None: services.json is byte-identical after sync (the long-syntax mount extracts to the same name/target/class entry), the volume entry shape is unchanged, and unparseable volume entries that were previously dropped silently now surface in unknowns - a reporting addition, not a contract change.
limitations: The extractor still implements only the Compose subset this repository uses: tmpfs/npipe mounts and single-path short-syntax entries are reported as unknowns, not classified
The unknown message says 'could not parse' even for a well-formed entry of an unsupported type; wording kept for consistency with the adjacent ports message

Shrink pass applied three findings (merged the two external-name sets into one built once, bound the long-syntax type lookup once, dropped an unused dummy Makefile target from the test helper); nothing further could be deleted because the module had no competing volume parser to consolidate
tools/repo_governance and docker-compose.yml are unassigned paths, so governance-impact's blast radius may be incomplete
reason: The services manifest extractor only understood short-form volume strings, so a long-syntax mount vanished from services.json while docker compose config still rendered it - silent omission that forced the 2026-08-25 sandboxd fix to keep short syntax and duplicate the workspace-root path by comment discipline instead of a YAML anchor
rollback: git revert of the single commit restores everything; no state lives outside the repository (no migration, no installed artifact, no volume rename - the fullstack_sandbox_workspaces volume and its data are untouched).
security_impact: None, deliberately: the extractor change only widens what the manifest records; the compose change re-expresses the sandboxd workspace mount in long syntax with a byte-identical rendered config (docker compose config output and governance-sync were both unchanged). The root-equivalent docker.sock mount is untouched.
summary: Parse Compose long-syntax volume mounts in the services extractor instead of silently dropping them
